title: The cost of LINQ, and IQueryable
sub: Buffering, allocations and SQL from lambdas
cards/0/body: To hand out the first element, OrderBy has to see them all — the smallest one might be last. Operators like this buffer: OrderBy, GroupBy, Reverse, Distinct (partly).
cards/1/task: Add OrderBy before Where and step to the end. How many numbers have to be read?
cards/2/q: Take(2) comes after OrderBy. Does Take save you from reading every element?
cards/2/options/0: No: OrderBy reads and sorts everything before handing out the first one
cards/2/options/2: Only if there is little data
cards/3/body:
Every capturing lambda is an object; every operator has its own enumerator. In everyday code this does not matter. In a hot loop that spins millions of times a second (a game, a server under load), a plain for loop can be several times faster.

LINQ gets faster with every .NET release — profile first, rewrite second.
cards/4/q: What is faster for checking "is there at least one element"?
cards/4/options/0: Any() — stops at the first one
cards/4/explain: For a list Count is cheap, but for a query or a database Any() does not scan everything.
cards/5/body: In Entity Framework, queries are IQueryable. A lambda there is not compiled into a method; it becomes an expression tree that EF translates into SQL.
cards/6/q: Inside an EF Where you call your own C# method IsVip(u), which SQL knows nothing about. What happens in EF Core?
cards/6/options/0: An exception: the expression cannot be translated to SQL
cards/6/options/1: EF quietly loads the whole table
cards/6/options/2: The method runs on the database server
cards/6/explain: Since EF Core 3.0, untranslatable expressions are no longer run quietly in memory — EF fails loudly.
cards/7/q: After which line does filtering happen in memory instead of in the database?
cards/7/explain: AsEnumerable switches to LINQ to Objects: from there on everything runs in C#, and the database sends every order over 100.
cards/8/pairs/0/1: The lambda is a regular method
cards/8/pairs/1/1: The lambda is an expression tree
cards/9/options/1: EF Core translates Where lambdas into SQL
cards/9/options/2: AsEnumerable moves the rest of the work into memory
cards/9/options/3: LINQ is always 100 times slower than for
cards/9/explain: There is a difference, but it is usually small and matters only on hot paths.
